title: Schedule a link's advices: back off, reconnect, park

blocks.text: The acquirer is replacing the store-and-forward queue of its network link. The old one caused four incidents last quarter:

items: after a 40-minute outage the link came back, and the queue sent nothing for another 12 minutes;
on a night when the link went down and up every few minutes, one reversal stayed at the front of the queue until morning, and the 300 completions behind it missed the clearing cut-off;
a voided sale was charged, because its completion reached the issuer after its reversal;
reversals that the network would no longer accept disappeared, and nobody could say which.

blocks.text: The network's specification for the link: after an advice's first unanswered attempt, wait the base delay before the next one, and twice as long after each further failure, but never longer than the cap. An advice gets at most `limit` attempts, and none at or after `window` from its first attempt. The constructor takes these four values.

`LinkSaf` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/LinkSaf.java` stores advices and hands its single sender what to send. `store`, `acknowledged` and the accessors are written. Write `due`, `failed`, `linkUp` and `waitAfter`; the comment on each says what it is for. About 25 lines in total.

cases.says: advices are handed out in the order they were stored, and an answered one leaves the queue
after an unanswered attempt the advice is not due at once, and when it is due again it is the repeat, otherwise unchanged
the wait after the first failure is the base delay, and it doubles after each further failure
the wait never grows beyond the cap
after dozens of failures the wait is still exactly the cap, never zero or negative
the network's time window runs from the first attempt, so time spent waiting for the link does not use it up, and no attempt goes out at or after it
a reconnect makes a waiting head due at once, still as a repeat, and does not give back the attempts it has used
while the head waits for its next attempt, nothing behind it is due
an advice that used its last attempt is kept among the parked advices in its stored form, and the next advice becomes due

origin.section: 20.4. After the Network's Limit an Entry Is Parked and Reported, Never Deleted

concepts: One sender per link takes only the head, so entries about one transaction reach the receiver in the order they were decided.
At the network's limit, in attempts or time from the first attempt, an entry is parked in its stored form and reported, and the next entry goes.
Later attempts are repeats; the wait doubles from a base up to a cap, and a reconnect makes the head due at once without resetting its count.
